thread:
alex: Heads-up — replay for tenant:acme is still queued and we crossed the sla-penalty threshold for yesterday's aggregates. Need a fast decision: downgrade tenant priority or fast-track a targeted backfill. Summary: ~120k missing agg rows, est cost ~ $4k, ETA on current queue ~ 4h.
maya: Ugh. Can we do a tiny dry-run on the 3 critical hourly buckets first? If output checks, promote to high-priority lane.
Tom: If we promote, we push other replays back. What's the SLA tradeoff? We might trigger another tenant's miss.
jen: Console side — we have the per-tenant "priority override" toggle, but it requires ops approval and an audit entry. @sam-op can you sign off for a one-off?
sam-op: oncall: short answer yes for a one-off. Need a cost cap and rollback plan. Also tag finance for potential invoice hit.
replay-bot: Backfill created: backfill-id=bf-4724-ACME mode=dryrun queued_by=maya
alex: Command I'd run locally to verify:
```
backfillctl run --tenant acme --from 2026-03-18T00:00Z --to 2026-03-18T03:00Z --mode=dryrun --output=artifact://tmp/bf-4724
```
maya: Running it now. I'll tail logs in #eng-platform-incidents. If the diff on key metrics is <0.1% we escalate. I'll post results.
Tom: Alternative plan: recompute only `agg_v2` with `--fast-path` (cheaper, less thorough). Risk: minor numeric drift vs full recompute.
jen: If we escalate, flip console flag `show-penalty-impact` so PM/finance see expected penalties and we surface a banner on tenant console saying "maintenance in progress".
sam-op: Approve high-priority for this window. Cost cap $5k. If we hit the cap, auto-rollback to standard lane and notify the owner.
replay-bot: backfill bf-4724-ACME-dryrun started -> logs: https://replay.redwood/logs/bf-4724-ACME | status: running
maya: dryrun finished. delta=0.07% on primary metrics, no schema drift. Artifacts: s3://replay-artifacts/bf-4724/diff.json
alex: Good. Recommend promote. Running:
```
backfillctl promote --id bf-4724-ACME --lane high --cost-cap 5000 --notify=owners,ops
```
replay-bot: bf-4724 promoted -> lane=high ETA=~45m. Notifying impacted tenants and creating audit entry.
Tom: Please log a short ops note: which knobs we used (priority-weight, cost-cap, lane) and any fallout. We should capture if the fast-path vs full recompute diverged.
jen: I'll file a console ticket to add an explicit audit trail for "priority override" and a temporary banner feature flag in the tenant UI.
sam-op: :thumbsup: Nice coordinated run. Keep monitoring for regressions. If anything looks off, pause and we can back out.
alex: Closing loop: once complete, I'll open a short postmortem focused on UX friction (ops approval path) and recommend an emergency toggle for small cost-limited fast-tracks.
maya: leaving logs and artifacts in the incident channel. Thanks everyone. :eyes:
